ports.changes: Use the upstream-pinned official SDK for transport/protocol. Adapt Hermes lifecycle invariants: owner task, initialization, capabilities-aware paginated listing, namespaced provenance, no replay of uncertain calls. Explicit configs replace all global home/profile discovery, callbacks, auth pools and reconnect loops. Optional stdio_start_guard checks host outcomes before launching a configured local server.

One ToolExecutor authority/effect boundary, endpoint-derived resource key independent of logical alias. Server descriptions and read-only hints cannot grant access. Optional host_resource and host_mutation_guard join stdio calls to terminal/files host effect protection; HTTP keeps endpoint scope.
Retain pure protocol metadata filtering, rename public strip function and add public argument type. Do not import original gateway media/cache host.

required_api.stdio: SDK safe OS environment allowlist plus explicit env; SDK-owned process group / Windows Job Object lifecycle

validation.transport_tested: real official SDK client and server over local stdio subprocess

limits: Handshake-era initialize negotiation only; modern-only server/discover, legacy SSE, OAuth, sampling and elicitation are not implemented.
Streamable HTTP transport is implemented against inspected SDK API, but this package validation used local stdio.
Tool results preserve protocol content and structured output; reserved protocol metadata is filtered. Native media are returned as protocol content, not automatically registered as QQ artifacts.
No runtime reconnect or automatic call replay. A faulted session needs explicit application lifecycle restart; unresolved effects remain blocked in StateStore.
MCP result handling currently retains complete protocol output in history; a separate task-scoped spillover/material integration is not implemented here.

hash_audit.note: Final frozen src/tests/tools byte inventory. Shared-file hashes cover application-owned integration changes too; source attribution applies only to the specifically described algorithms/behaviors, not every line of a shared target. Original validation observations are retained.
